content.title: About
content.content: Barley flour is a whole‑grain product made by grinding barley kernels. It has a light brown color, a mild nutty aroma, and a lower gluten content than wheat flour, making it popular in gluten‑reduced and health‑focused recipes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Barley is one of the oldest cultivated grains, grown for more than 10,000 years.
Barley flour is rich in beta‑glucans, which help lower cholesterol levels.
Compared with wheat flour, barley flour has a lower glycemic index.
Ancient civilizations used barley as a staple for bread and porridge.
Barley flour is often used in brewing to enhance flavor and foam stability.

items.title: High in beta‑glucans
items.content: Beta‑glucans support heart health, help regulate blood sugar, and boost immunity.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Barley provides thiamine, niacin, and folate, essential for metabolism.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: The flour supplies magnesium, phosphorus, iron, and zinc, important for bones and the nervous system.

items.title: Low gluten content
items.content: Suitable for people with mild gluten sensitivity, though not completely gluten‑free.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber in barley flour promotes regular bowel movements and helps prevent constipation.

items.title: Cereal allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to barley.

items.title: Gluten presence
items.content: People with celiac disease should avoid barley flour because it contains gluten.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: High phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking or sprouting grains can mitigate this.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Barley flour is used in breads, flatbreads, pancakes, cookies, and cakes. It blends well with other flours, improving texture and flavor. It can also be added to porridge, soups, and sauces as a thickener.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the flour in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation.
